title: Johns Hopkins University (JHU)
summary: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) is a university in Baltimore. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with JHU.

sections.heading: What JHU is known for
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) is a private nonprofit institution known for its rigorous academic environment and selective admissions process, with an admission rate of approximately 6.44%. The university enrolls around 5,693 undergraduate students, reflecting its commitment to a focused and engaged student body. JHU is particularly recognized for its strong emphasis on health-related programs, which constitute about 9.76% of its academic offerings. While the university does not have a significant business program share, its reputation is largely built on excellence in health sciences and research. As a private nonprofit university, JHU maintains a distinctive position in higher education, combining a selective admission process with specialized academic strengths.

sections.heading: Key strengths
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) is a private nonprofit institution distinguished by its specialized academic strengths. sections.heading: Popular majors
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) offers a range of academic programs with notable concentrations in health and computer-related fields. sections.heading: Undergraduate admissions
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) maintains a highly selective undergraduate admissions process, with an admission rate of approximately 6.44%. The university seeks students who demonstrate exceptional academic achievement and potential. The average SAT score for admitted students is 1553, reflecting the competitive nature of the applicant pool. While specific details about the use of the Common Application or early decision policies are not provided, JHU's admissions process emphasizes a holistic review of each candidate's qualifications.

sections.heading: International admissions
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) welcomes applications from international students across its various programs. The university evaluates international applicants through the same holistic admissions process used for domestic candidates, considering academic records, standardized test scores, and other personal achievements. While specific international admissions statistics and requirements are not detailed, JHU provides resources to assist international applicants in navigating the application process and understanding financial aid opportunities.

sections.heading: How to read JHU tuition
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) charges a tuition fee of $65,230 for both in-state and out-of-state students, reflecting a uniform tuition policy regardless of residency. The total cost of attendance, which includes tuition along with additional expenses such as fees, room, board, and other personal costs, amounts to $85,947. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and families anticipate the financial commitment required for enrollment at JHU.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) offers financial aid to support students in managing the cost of attendance. Approximately 19.49% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies aimed at assisting low-income undergraduates. Among students who complete their degrees, the median debt incurred is $10,250, indicating the typical loan amount graduates carry. For more detailed information on financial aid options and cost estimates, prospective students can visit the university's official website at www.jhu.edu or consult the College Scorecard profile at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?162928.

sections.heading: Housing and dining
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) provides housing options for students both on and off campus, with associated room and board costs reflecting these choices. The estimated annual expense for living on campus, including room and board, is approximately $20,150. For students opting to live off campus, the combined cost of room and board is lower, at about $14,933 per year. These figures help students and families plan for the financial aspects of housing and dining during their studies at JHU.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) demonstrates strong career outcomes for its graduates, with a high completion rate of approximately 93.78% within 150% of the expected time. Graduates tend to achieve substantial earnings, with median salaries reaching $86,306 six years after enrollment and increasing slightly to $87,555 ten years post-enrollment. The median debt for students who complete their degrees is relatively moderate, at $10,250, indicating manageable loan burdens for many graduates. These figures reflect JHU's ability to prepare students effectively for the workforce and support their long-term financial success.

sections.heading: Internships and research
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) is renowned for its strong emphasis on research, providing students with numerous opportunities to engage in cutting-edge projects across various disciplines. The university fosters a collaborative environment where undergraduate and graduate students can participate in research initiatives that contribute to advancements in health sciences, engineering, and other fields. JHU's commitment to research excellence is supported by extensive resources and faculty expertise, enabling students to gain valuable hands-on experience. For more information on research and internship opportunities, prospective students can visit the university's official website at www.jhu.edu.

sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Johns Hopkins University (JHU) exhibits a diverse student body with a gender distribution of approximately 45.06% men and 54.94% women. The racial and ethnic composition includes about 19.5% White, 8.33% Black, 18.67% Hispanic, and 29.37% Asian students, reflecting a broad representation of backgrounds. Additionally, nearly 19.49% of students receive Pell Grants, indicating a significant portion of the undergraduate population benefits from federal financial aid aimed at supporting low-income students. This diversity contributes to a dynamic campus environment that fosters inclusive learning and engagement.
